title: My Husband Begged Me to Carry His Gay Boss's Baby for a Promotion, Until a Late-Night Phone Call Revealed Who the Baby Was Really For
fb_text:
My husband begged me to carry a baby for his gay boss, saying it could help him get promoted. I agreed, believing I was building a better future for our family. Then, months into my pregnancy, I overheard a conversation that revealed his true intentions. What I heard him say made me physically sick.

PART 1

The first time my husband brought up surrogacy, I was cutting his birthday cake.

His boss, Everett, wanted a child. He was gay, single, and looking for a woman willing to carry a baby for him.

Apparently my husband had already told him how much I'd loved being pregnant with our daughter.

"Wait, you talked about my pregnancies with your boss?"

"Only good things." He slipped his arms around my waist. "He said we were lucky to have Daisy and such a happy family."

I remember leaning into him, comforted by his words.

A week later, he brought it up again.

Everett had invited us to dinner. My husband explained it would simply be a chance to talk, with no obligation on my part.

When I hesitated, he took my hand.

"He's thinking about making me regional director. I'm not saying helping him guarantees the promotion, but it might show him how committed and trustworthy I am."

Money problems had already put a lot of strain on our marriage. Our mortgage had gone up, and the expensive car my husband insisted he needed for work was swallowing almost all our savings.

"Why don't we sell the car first?"

He pulled his hand away immediately.

"I already feel like I'm letting you and Daisy down. Do you really have to keep reminding me?"

Before I knew it, I was the one comforting him.

From then on, he talked less and less about Everett's wish to become a father, and more and more about how the promotion could improve our lives.

He promised he could stop working weekends, take us on a real vacation at last, and buy us a new washing machine instead of making us restart our broken one in the middle of every cycle.

"You keep telling me you miss me," he reminded me. "I'm trying to find a way to spend more time with my family."

I still loved my husband.

And I missed the marriage we used to have.

In the end, I said yes.

We went through medical exams, attended counseling sessions, and filled out all the paperwork. Every time someone asked whether anyone was pressuring me, I said no.

My husband kept telling me this decision was entirely mine.

I wanted that to be true.

But every time I thought about backing out, he would sit silently at the kitchen table, eyes fixed on our unpaid bills, until I felt guilty.

The second embryo transfer worked.

When the pregnancy was confirmed, my husband burst into tears.

Then his behavior changed.

He became so attentive that I began to hope this arrangement might even save our marriage.

He carried the groceries, came with me to my medical appointments, and rested his hand on my rounded belly while we watched TV.

One evening, he felt the baby move.

He smiled at me in a way I hadn't seen in years.

I put my hand over his.

"I missed this version of you so much," I whispered.

By the time I reached twenty-four weeks, I had started to believe we were truly finding our way back to each other.

Then, one night, I woke up thirsty.

My husband's side of the bed was empty.

I saw a light on downstairs and heard his voice coming from the kitchen.

I walked toward the door, thinking I'd simply get a glass of water.

Then I heard him laugh.

"She really believes this whole thing is about my promotion."

I stopped dead, my hand pressed against the door frame.

He paused to listen to whoever was on the other end.

"No, she suspects nothing. Honestly, she's even a lot happier lately."

I stood frozen, barefoot in the hallway.

The refrigerator hummed behind his voice as he listened to the person on the phone.

When he spoke again, his voice was strangely soft.

"I want that too. But we have to wait until after she gives birth. She still has no idea who this baby is really for."

Instinctively, I pressed my hand against my belly.

The baby moved beneath my palm.

Then my husband said something so terrible that I clapped my hand over my mouth in horror.

article_html:
My husband begged me to carry a baby for his gay boss, promising it might help him get promoted. I said yes, believing I was building a better future for our family. Then, one night, I overheard a phone call that changed everything.

How It Began

The first time my husband mentioned surrogacy, I was cutting his birthday cake. His boss, Everett, was gay and single, and he wanted a child. My husband had already told him how much I'd loved being pregnant with our daughter, Daisy.

A week later, he raised it again. Everett had invited us to dinner, he said, just to talk, with no obligation. Then he took my hand and told me Everett was considering him for regional director. Helping might show how committed and trustworthy he was.

Money was already straining our marriage. The mortgage had gone up, and the expensive car he insisted he needed for work was eating our savings. When I suggested selling it, he pulled his hand away. "I already feel like I'm letting you and Daisy down. Do you really have to keep reminding me?"

Suddenly I was the one comforting him.

Saying Yes

He began talking less about Everett's dream of fatherhood and more about what the promotion could give us: no more working weekends, a real vacation, a washing machine that didn't have to be restarted in the middle of every cycle. "You keep telling me you miss me," he said. "I'm trying to spend more time with my family."

I still loved him. I missed the marriage we used to have. So I agreed.

We went through medical exams and counseling and signed every form. Each time I was asked whether anyone was pressuring me, I said no. My husband insisted the choice was mine. But whenever I wavered, he would sit silently at the kitchen table staring at our unpaid bills until guilt won.

The second embryo transfer worked. My husband cried when the pregnancy was confirmed, and then he became the man I remembered, carrying groceries, coming to appointments, resting his hand on my belly in front of the TV. When he felt the baby kick, he smiled the way he used to years ago.

"I missed this version of you so much," I whispered.

The Kitchen Light

At twenty-four weeks, I woke up thirsty and found his side of the bed empty. A light was on downstairs. I heard him laugh.

"She really believes this whole thing is about my promotion."

I froze in the hallway, barefoot, my hand on the door frame.

"No, she suspects nothing. She's even a lot happier lately." Then, softly: "I want that too. But we have to wait until after she gives birth. She still has no idea who this baby is really for."

The baby moved under my palm. Then he said something so cruel that I covered my mouth to keep from making a sound: once the baby was born, the plan was for him and the woman on the phone to keep the child and cut Everett out entirely. The promotion had never mattered.

What I Did Next

I crept back upstairs and lay awake until morning, shaking, my hand on my belly. By sunrise I knew what I had to do.

While my husband was at work, I called the counselor from our surrogacy sessions and asked for an urgent meeting. I told her everything I had heard. She helped me contact a lawyer and, with my permission, Everett.

Everett was stunned. My husband had never told him I was hesitant, and he had never mentioned any promotion. Everett was kind and horrified, and he promised me this baby would be loved and protected. I believed him.

That evening, I told my husband I knew. He denied it at first, then said I had misunderstood, then finally went quiet. The silence told me everything. I packed a bag, took Daisy, and went to stay with my sister.

The Ending

The agreement we had signed protected everyone, and with my lawyer's help the legal path was clear. I carried the pregnancy to term, and when the baby arrived, I placed him in Everett's arms. He wept. So did I, but this time from relief.

My husband lost far more than a promotion. I filed for divorce, and Daisy and I moved into a smaller place, with a washing machine that works.

Everett still sends photos of his son. Every time, I'm reminded that I did one thing right: I listened to my own instincts, even when the voice in the kitchen was the one I loved most.

source.text:
Mon mari m’a suppliée de porter un enfant pour son patron homosexuel, en prétendant que cela pourrait l’aider à obtenir une promotion. J’ai fini par accepter, persuadée de faire quelque chose pour offrir un avenir meilleur à notre famille. Mais, quelques mois après le début de ma grossesse, j’ai surpris une conversation qui m’a révélé ses véritables intentions. Ce que je l’ai entendu dire m’a littéralement donné la nausée.

PARTIE 1

La première fois que mon mari m’a parlé de gestation pour autrui, j’étais en train de couper son gâteau d’anniversaire.

Son patron, Everett, désirait avoir un enfant. Il était homosexuel, célibataire et cherchait une femme disposée à porter un bébé pour lui.

Apparemment, mon mari lui avait déjà raconté à quel point j’avais aimé être enceinte de notre fille.

« Attends, tu as parlé de mes grossesses à ton patron ? »

« Seulement en bien. » Il passa ses bras autour de ma taille. « Il a dit que nous avions de la chance d’avoir Daisy et une famille aussi heureuse. »

Je me souviens m’être blottie contre lui, rassurée par ses paroles.

Une semaine plus tard, il remit le sujet sur la table.

Everett nous avait invités à dîner. Mon mari m’expliqua que ce serait simplement l’occasion d’en discuter, sans aucune obligation de ma part.

Lorsque j’hésitai, il me prit la main.

« Il envisage de me nommer directeur régional. Je ne dis pas que l’aider me garantira cette promotion, mais cela pourrait lui montrer à quel point je suis engagé et digne de confiance. »

Les problèmes financiers avaient déjà provoqué beaucoup de tensions dans notre mariage. Notre crédit immobilier avait augmenté et la voiture coûteuse que mon mari prétendait indispensable pour son travail engloutissait presque toutes nos économies.

« Pourquoi ne pas vendre la voiture d’abord ? »

Il retira immédiatement sa main.

« J’ai déjà l’impression de vous décevoir, toi et Daisy. Tu dois vraiment continuer à me le rappeler ? »

Avant même de m’en rendre compte, c’était moi qui étais en train de le réconforter.

À partir de ce moment-là, il parla de moins en moins du désir d’Everett de devenir père et de plus en plus de la façon dont cette promotion pourrait améliorer notre vie.

Il me promit qu’il pourrait arrêter de travailler le week-end, nous emmener enfin en véritables vacances et nous acheter une nouvelle machine à laver au lieu de devoir relancer notre vieille machine cassée au milieu de chaque cycle.

« Tu n’arrêtes pas de me dire que ma présence te manque », me rappela-t-il. « J’essaie de trouver un moyen de passer davantage de temps avec ma famille. »

J’aimais toujours mon mari.

Et notre mariage d’autrefois me manquait.

Finalement, j’acceptai.

Nous passâmes des examens médicaux, suivîmes des séances de conseil et remplîmes tous les documents nécessaires. Chaque fois qu’on me demandait si quelqu’un me mettait la pression, je répondais non.

Mon mari me répétait sans cesse que cette décision m’appartenait entièrement.

Je voulais que ce soit vrai.

Mais chaque fois que je pensais à faire marche arrière, il s’asseyait silencieusement à la table de la cuisine, les yeux fixés sur nos factures impayées, jusqu’à ce que je me sente coupable.

Le deuxième transfert d’embryon réussit.

Lorsque la grossesse fut confirmée, mon mari éclata en sanglots.

Puis son comportement changea.

Il devint tellement attentionné que je commençai à espérer que cet arrangement pourrait même sauver notre couple.

Il portait les courses, m’accompagnait à mes rendez-vous médicaux et posait sa main sur mon ventre arrondi pendant que nous regardions la télévision.

Un soir, il sentit le bébé bouger.

Il me sourit d’une manière que je n’avais pas vue depuis des années.

Je posai ma main sur la sienne.

« Cette version de toi m’avait tellement manqué », lui murmurai-je.

Lorsque j’atteignis la vingt-quatrième semaine de grossesse, j’avais commencé à croire que nous étions réellement en train de nous retrouver.

Puis, une nuit, je me réveillai avec une sensation de soif.

Le côté du lit où dormait mon mari était vide.

J’aperçus une lumière allumée en bas et entendis sa voix venant de la cuisine.

Je me dirigeai vers la porte, pensant simplement aller boire un verre d’eau.

Puis je l’entendis rire.

« Elle croit vraiment que toute cette histoire concerne ma promotion. »

Je m’arrêtai net, la main posée contre le cadre de la porte.

Il marqua une pause pour écouter la réponse de son interlocuteur.

« Non, elle ne se doute absolument de rien. En fait, elle est même beaucoup plus heureuse ces derniers temps. »

Je restai immobile, pieds nus dans le couloir.

Le réfrigérateur ronronnait derrière sa voix tandis qu’il écoutait la personne au téléphone.

Lorsqu’il reprit la parole, sa voix était étrangement douce.

« Moi aussi, je le veux. Mais nous devons attendre qu’elle accouche. Elle n’a toujours aucune idée de la personne à qui ce bébé est réellement destiné. »

Instinctivement, je plaquai ma main contre mon ventre.

Le bébé bougea sous ma paume.

Puis mon mari prononça quelque chose de si terrible que je portai ma main à ma bouche, horrifiée.
